can_answer: partly: the file can show how recorded crash counts are distributed by clock time, but it has no traffic-volume or travel-exposure denominator for comparing crash risk
metric: annual share of recorded crashes by time-of-day group
denominator: all recorded crashes in that calendar year (count of rows)
population: police-reported NYC motor-vehicle crashes in calendar years fully covered by the file
filters: exclude calendar years not fully covered by the file
classify crash_time 20:00–23:59 and 00:01–05:59 as night; 06:00–19:59 as day; show 00:00 and missing crash_time in a separate ambiguous/unclassified group
years: all fully covered calendar years in the file, determined from crash_date coverage in the data check
grouping: calendar year and night/day/ambiguous-or-unclassified time group

data_check.coverage: The file spans 2012-07-01 through 2026-06-11; 2012 (100,545 rows) and 2026 (36,424 rows) are partial calendar years and are excluded. Fully covered years are 2013–2025.
data_check.time_quality: In 2013–2025, crash_time is NULL on 0 rows. Midnight is recorded 23,787 times in those years, including a sharp increase from 24 in 2015 to 2,895 in 2016; the typed TIME column cannot distinguish actual midnight crashes from possible default-coded times.
data_check.decision: Retain all crashes in the annual denominator and show midnight and missing times as a separate ambiguous/unclassified group rather than assigning possible defaults to night.

limitations: The data check excludes partial years 2012 and 2026 and finds no NULL crash_time values in 2013–2025, but midnight occurs 23,787 times and may include default-coded values, so it is shown separately. Crash records contain no traffic-volume or trip-exposure denominator, so the chart describes recorded crash distribution rather than comparative crash risk.
